evals.prompt: We're building a mobile banking app. Write user stories for push notifications — specifically when a transaction hits the account. Users should be able to opt in and out.
evals.expected_output: Well-structured EARS-Lite user stories with hierarchical numbering (1.1 format), priority field, 'As a [persona]' headers, and coverage of the opt-out edge case. Save to aidlc-docs/story-artifacts/ after user approval.
expectations: Output uses EARS-Lite format with WHEN/IF/WHILE + SHALL keywords (not plain bullet points)
Output contains hierarchical EARS-Lite numbering in the form X.X (e.g., 1.1, 1.2)
Output contains a Priority field with High, Medium, or Low value
Output contains a user story header in 'As a [persona], I want [goal], so that [benefit]' format
Output covers the opt-out or disable notifications scenario (edge case)

evals.prompt: Add export to the admin dashboard
evals.expected_output: Skill should choose clarification-first behavior, ask the missing export questions, and wait instead of pretending the artifact is final.
expectations: Output raises clarifying questions BEFORE presenting user stories
Output mentions at least one export format option (CSV, PDF, Excel, JSON, or similar)
Output asks about delivery mode such as on-demand vs scheduled or equivalent
Output does not present a finalized user-story artifact before the ambiguity is resolved
Question options are concrete rather than vague

evals.prompt: I'm building a SaaS project management tool. I need user stories for the onboarding flow — creating an account, setting up the first project, and inviting team members.
evals.expected_output: Multiple user stories covering account creation, first project setup, and team invitation as separate user-visible outcomes, with EARS-Lite acceptance criteria and sequencing notes where useful.
expectations: Output contains at least 3 distinct user stories (US-001, US-002, US-003 or similar numbering)
At least one story addresses account creation or registration
At least one story addresses first project setup or project creation
At least one story addresses team invitation or adding team members
Output uses EARS-Lite format with WHEN/IF/WHILE + SHALL keywords
All stories include a Priority field
Stories are split by user-visible value rather than frontend/backend layers
Output includes dependency notes or equivalent sequencing guidance if order matters

evals.prompt: Use the attached foundation docs. Create user stories for an offline inspection checklist with photo attachments and sync recovery for field visits.
evals.expected_output: Stories should reuse foundation personas exactly, incorporate offline-first and image-size constraints, and reference existing UX components when they improve clarity.
expectations: Output reuses the exact persona names from the attached project overview rather than inventing new ones
Acceptance criteria mention offline behavior or sync recovery consistent with the attached architecture docs
Acceptance criteria mention the 10MB image limit or an equivalent attached technical constraint
Output references an existing UI component from the attached UX guideline only where relevant
Output uses EARS-Lite format with hierarchical numbering

evals.prompt: Use the attached foundation docs. Write user stories for a public marketing landing page and a customer referral program.
evals.expected_output: Skill should notice the request conflicts with the attached product scope and flag it before generating in-scope stories.
expectations: Output explicitly flags the request as outside or beyond the attached product scope
Output offers a path forward such as clarifying whether the scope should be expanded
Output does not silently present the request as if it were already in scope

evals.prompt: I need a rough draft for admin audit export. Make reasonable assumptions and proceed.
evals.expected_output: Skill should not generate under unresolved assumptions. It should ask for the missing actor, export format, schedule/delivery mode, scope, or success criteria before writing stories.
expectations: Output raises clarifying questions BEFORE presenting user stories
Output treats 'make reasonable assumptions' as insufficient when unresolved decisions are missing
Output asks about at least one missing decision such as actor, export format, delivery mode, scope, or success criteria
Output does not present a finalized user-story artifact before the ambiguity is resolved
Output does not use an artifact section as a substitute for clarification

evals.prompt: Write user stories for shipment document upload with validation for an Operations User uploading PDF shipping documents from a shipment detail page. Use --template checklist.
evals.expected_output: Skill should generate user stories using the checklist template, with normal user story metadata and categorized checklist acceptance criteria.
expectations: Output uses the checklist template instead of hierarchical EARS-Lite sections or a Given/When/Then table
Each story keeps the normal User Story line and Priority field rather than turning story metadata into bullets
Acceptance Criteria are written as Markdown checklist items with - [ ]
Acceptance Criteria use the shallowest useful trace ID depth, such as 1, 1.1, or 1.1.1 depending on grouping complexity
Checklist criteria are grouped under numbered category headings by default and scenario subheadings only when useful
Acceptance criteria remain testable and include at least one validation or error scenario
Output does not use a Markdown table for acceptance criteria

evals.prompt: Write user stories for commodity lookup from the booking screen for a Booking Agent selecting a commodity code during shipment booking. Use --template given-when-then-table.
evals.expected_output: Skill should generate user stories with acceptance criteria grouped by numbered Feature headings and Markdown tables using No., Scenario, Given, When, and Then columns.
expectations: Output uses the given-when-then-table template
Acceptance Criteria are grouped under numbered Feature headings such as Feature 1
Acceptance Criteria are formatted as Markdown tables with columns No., Scenario, Given, When, and Then
No. values use feature-prefixed numbering such as 1.1, 1.2, and 2.1
Each table row includes a concise scenario name in the Scenario column
Given cells describe screen, state, or preconditions
When cells describe user actions or system triggers
Then cells describe visible results or system behavior
The table includes at least one negative path or empty-result scenario

evals.prompt: Create and save standalone Inception user stories for shipment exception triage from an operations queue for Operations Users triaging exception status, assignee, priority, and resolution notes. Use --template checklist. This is a story-artifacts output, not a spec-driven requirements.md.
evals.expected_output: Skill should scaffold the standalone story artifact with the requirements-engineering wrapper, use the shared checklist story-block format, save under aidlc-docs/story-artifacts/, run the Product Owner review gate before user handoff, and avoid spec-driven requirements wrapper sections or Phase 2 next-step text.
expectations: A story artifact file is created under aidlc-docs/story-artifacts/ with a three-digit prefix and suffix _user_stories.md
The assistant presents the saved artifact path as the working draft for feedback and future updates
Output includes a '## Overview' section before '## User stories'
Output uses checklist acceptance criteria with Markdown - [ ] items and stable IDs such as 1.1 or 2.1
Output keeps normal story metadata such as User Story and Priority outside the checklist items
Output includes standalone story-artifact sections only when useful, such as User stories or Dependency Notes

After the first complete saved draft, output indicates Product Owner review ran with a PASS, FIX_BEFORE_USER_REVIEW, or NEEDS_USER_DECISION verdict, or explicitly states delegated subagent review was unavailable and an inline review checklist was used instead
Product Owner review is review-only: the response does not claim the subagent edited the artifact directly, and clear blocking fixes are applied by the parent before user handoff
The assistant does not ask the user for artifact feedback until the Product Owner review gate has passed or a required user decision is surfaced
Output does not include a '# Requirements:' heading
Output does not include spec metadata fields such as Unit, Created, or User Stories at the document top
Output does not include a 'Next Steps' section instructing the user to proceed to Phase 2 design

evals.prompt: Add user stories for an external feedback survey feature.
evals.expected_output: Skill should clarify all artifact-shaping survey decisions before generating or saving stories, including trigger moments, cooldown or frequency, disable behavior, and privacy or telemetry boundaries.
expectations: Output raises clarifying questions BEFORE presenting or saving user stories
Output asks which moments or events should trigger the survey
Output asks about at least two of: frequency/cooldown, disable or opt-out behavior, privacy/telemetry/data boundaries
Output marks recommended options with (Recommended)
Output does not present a finalized user-story artifact before these decisions are resolved
Output does not hide unresolved survey behavior behind generic configurable wording; open values are either asked about or absent, not papered over

evals.prompt: This workspace's .mtv-aidlc/extension-config.json is attached; note it sets aidlcDocsPath to docs/aidlc. Create and save user stories for password reset via emailed link for registered customers. In scope: requesting a reset from the login screen, receiving a time-limited link by email that expires after 30 minutes, setting a new password that meets the existing password policy, and invalidating old sessions after a successful reset. Out of scope: SMS reset and security questions. Use --template default.
evals.expected_output: Skill should honor the configured aidlcDocsPath: the artifact is scaffolded and saved under docs/aidlc/story-artifacts/, not a hardcoded aidlc-docs/ root, with compliant frontmatter.
expectations: The story artifact is created under docs/aidlc/story-artifacts/ (the configured aidlcDocsPath), not under aidlc-docs/
The saved path presented to the user matches the configured docs root
The artifact frontmatter includes intent and source_artifacts keys
Output uses EARS-Lite format with hierarchical numbering and Priority fields
Acceptance criteria cover the 30-minute link expiry and session invalidation behaviors

evals.prompt:
We're cleaning up our old backlog. Normalize these three Jira tickets into a story artifact:

PROJ-101 'Export orders to CSV': Users need to export their orders. Should be user friendly and fast.
PROJ-102 'Order export permissions': Only managers can export. Other roles get an error message.
PROJ-103 'CSV export backend endpoint': Build a /api/orders/export endpoint that returns text/csv.
evals.expected_output: Skill should treat this as brownfield import: map tickets to user-visible stories, fold the backend-endpoint ticket into the export story instead of keeping a technical-layer story, preserve Jira IDs in Related Jira fields, and flag or clarify the untestable 'user friendly and fast' wording instead of inventing metrics.
expectations: Source ticket IDs (PROJ-101, PROJ-102, PROJ-103) are preserved in Related Jira fields or an explicit ticket-to-story mapping
PROJ-103 is merged into the user-visible export story rather than kept as a separate backend/technical-layer story
The vague 'user friendly and fast' wording is clarified with the user or explicitly surfaced as an open decision, not silently replaced with invented metrics
No source ticket is dropped silently: every ticket is mapped to a story, merged, or flagged
Manager-only access and the error for other roles from PROJ-102 appear as acceptance criteria
